doc: The host's RPC (kith-serve /api, the relay and the local socket): what the host answers and what desktop, web and iOS send it. This part covers what an invited person (a member) and a bot guest may call; the owner's methods follow. Times are epoch milliseconds. Additive only: see serve/contract/README.md.

EntryKind.doc: What a transcript entry is. One this version doesn't know is its own kind: an app skips it.

BotKind.doc: A roster row: an agent bot, or a group chat of bots and the user.

BotStatus.doc: What a bot is doing right now. One this version doesn't know reads as idle: no spinner.

Permission.doc: A bot's permission mode: Claude Code's own, passed to the agent unchanged. One this version doesn't know is its own state: the app shows no mode as picked.

AgentRole.doc: What an invited person is in an agent they hold: a member (the member preset) or a guest. One this version doesn't know is guest, the least.

Device.doc: What kind of computer the host runs on (the apps' computer icon). One this version doesn't know is a desktop.

BotProvider.doc: Whose bot a bot guest is. The host stores other for anything else, and so does a consumer.

BotGuestState.doc: Where a bot guest is in its life (denied and revoked are final). One this version doesn't know is its own state: the bot is not active.

ProjectsBy.doc: Who set a thread's project set: the bot's settings (pinned), the host's inference, or the person's correction. One this version doesn't know reads as inferred.

MessageVia.doc: How a message was made, when not typed: spoken in a voice call. The host reads any other value, or none, as typed.

CitationError.doc: Why a citation link didn't open. The same answer whether the thread is someone else's, missing, forgotten or the link malformed.

ConversationState.doc: Where a bot's conversation stands: a turn running, a turn waiting for the owner to approve a step, asks waiting behind a running turn, the last ask stopped, or nothing going on. One this version doesn't know reads as running: a turn is over only when done says so.

BotEntryKind.doc: A transcript entry as a bot sees it: its ask, the agent's words, a notice that ends the turn with an error, or a bare wait for the owner to approve a step. One this version doesn't know is its own kind: a bot skips it.

RoomConversationState.doc: Where a room conversation is in its life. One this version doesn't know reads as ended: the app stops drawing a live line.

RoomConversationEnd.doc: Why a room conversation is over. One this version doesn't know is its own word: the app shows it plainly as over.

RoomSpeakerKind.doc: What speaks in a room conversation: one of the room's own agents, or an outside bot. One this version doesn't know reads as agent.

BotErrorCode.doc: The machine word in an error answer of the bot guest methods, {status, message, code}, which a bot acts on (apps ignore it; tooMany answers a person making one bot too many). One this version doesn't know is its own: a bot acts on the answer's HTTP status.

Empty.doc: An answer with nothing in it.

StoreHealth.doc: Whether the host can save: writable is false while the disk is full or read-only; entries wait in memory meanwhile.

GrantedAgent.doc: An agent an invited person holds, for the apps' New chat.

Hello.doc: The connection handshake. A member gets the names and keys only, and the agents they hold; the fields marked owner's are the owner's alone and are typed with the owner's methods.

KithCard.doc: An agent's card as a member sees it: only what it says about itself.

KithInfo.doc: An agent's card (null for a chat that isn't a Kith agent's). The owner's card is the whole of `kith --info-json`, and error is the owner's.

WorkingLane.doc: A place a bot works in: a chat (its own or a group) and, in a thread, the thread's root.

BotGuestRef.doc: The outside bot behind a bot guest's chat.

Bot.doc: A roster row: an agent bot or a group. A member never gets cwd, command or folder (where it works on the owner's computer); a group has no folder, sharedMemory or memoryRev.

Entry.doc: One line of a chat's transcript. Its data is the kind's own and is not in this contract yet.

Entries.doc: A page of a chat or a thread. folder is where it works on this computer: the owner's alone. conversation is the room conversation of that lane (the chat's main lane, or the thread) that was opened last, so a reconnecting app can draw the live line; null when the lane never had one. A host from before it leaves the field out.

RoomConversation.doc: Where a room conversation stands: what one person message to a group set going. budget is the turns that message granted and left what remains; current is whoever speaks now and waitUntil (unix ms) when an outside bot's turn times out; endedWhy says why it is over (spent: the turns ran out, quiet: a round where everyone passed, stopped: a person's Stop, idle: nobody moved it for a day, newer: a newer person message took the lane); opening is the entry of the person message that opened it. lane is the thread's id, null for the room's main lane. endedWhy is null for a conversation that is open or that ended before hosts kept the reason.

RoomSpeaker.doc: Who speaks now in a room conversation.

ConversationEvent.doc: The `conversation` event the owner's apps (and no one else) get on the event stream: a room conversation's RoomConversation fields, sent when it opens, at each charge, each change of speaker and when it ends.

MaybeEntry.doc: The entry a call changed; null when it wasn't saved.

CallEnded.doc: A call's line with its length; absent for a call that never connected.

Uploaded.doc: The file, once its last chunk is in; null before.

UploadChunk.doc: A chunk of a sent file: base64 data, and the file's whole size.

PermissionAnswered.doc: closed: the card was already answered or is gone, so this answer changed nothing.

Project.doc: A project folder. A member gets its id and name; its folders on this computer (path, paths, parent, exists) are the owner's.

Projects.doc: The projects shared with a member (the owner's: all of them). error says why there are none; the owner's.

ThreadProjects.doc: The project set a thread runs under now; empty when it has none. pinned: the bot's settings fix it.

ThreadProjectsSet.doc: The thread's project set after a correction; changed is false when it already was that.

Citation.doc: A kith://thread/<id>#entry=<seq> link opened: the thread, the cited entry's seq and id (at), and its entries; or only error.

LinkCode.doc: The code that links a Telegram, Discord or Slack account to the caller's person.

CallAccepted.doc: The chat the accepted call belongs to.

BotInviteCreated.doc: A bot guest's invite: the link (web and kith://), and share, the text to paste into the bot.

Revoked.doc: revoked is false when it already was.

BotLimits.doc: A bot's limits. turnTimeoutS is how long a room waits for its post when it is a member's turn (30 to 3600, default 300; a miss is a pass). wakeProfile is the kith-auth profile the host pushes a wake through at that turn (null: no wake, so the turn is a pass). Absent from an older host.

BotGuest.doc: A bot guest. personId and conversations are the computer owner's.

BotGuestAnswer.doc: The bot after the change; null once it is gone.

BotOwner.doc: A bot's owner, by the name people know them by.

BotSelf.doc: A bot's own state, owner and agents. The agents are the live answer: none until the bot is allowed, and one its owner lost is gone at once.

PeerAgent.doc: One agent a paired computer may ask: its name, and the bot's display name when it has one.

PeerAgents.doc: The agents a paired computer may ask here.

HandleRevoke.doc: One person known only by a chat handle (`telegram:123`), revoked or restored, and when (ms). The latest change of a handle wins on every computer.

HandleRevokes.doc: Every handle revoke or undo the sender knows; the answer is the receiver's own list, so both ends hold the latest of each.

BotProof.doc: Where the bot stands once its key showed the invite token. A repeat (the key was already proven) answers the state only.

BotAsked.doc: An ask taken: its conversation, its entry and turn, and whether it runs now or waits (queued: how many asks wait in the conversation). A retry with the same clientNonce answers the same, marked duplicate, and sends nothing.

BotPosted.doc: A post into a room, stored: its entry and turn. replied: it was the member's reply that the room was waiting for. late: it is kept in the room but woke nobody and was not charged (the conversation is over, or the epoch or turnKey is no longer current); lateWhy says which: stopped (after a Stop), newer (a newer person message moved the epoch), ended (the conversation ended: spent, quiet or idle), noTurn (a keyed post nobody waits for any more). unprompted: a post with no turn key while no conversation is open, kept, not late, and it woke nobody and cost nothing. A retry with the same clientNonce and text answers the same, marked duplicate.

BotRoom.doc: A room as a bot member reads it: the entries after the cursor (the newest few on a first read), the room's newest conversation and its epoch (what a post names), and the cursor to read from next.

BotSender.doc: Who sent an ask: the bot, and the person it spoke for when it said.

BotEntry.doc: A transcript entry as a bot sees it: never a thought, a tool call, a plan, an attachment, or a permission card's tool. sender is on an ask a bot sent, final on the agent's words, error on a notice.

BotThread.doc: A bot's conversation since afterSeq. done: the last ask has its final answer, an error notice, or was taken back; turn is the last ask's.

BotConversation.doc: One of a bot's conversations, with the external ref it gave it.

hello.doc: The connection handshake; answered to a member or a bot without paths, addresses, backends or screen state, with the agents they hold.

kithInfo.doc: An agent's card, for a chat that is theirs.

startChat.doc: Their own chat with an agent they hold, one per agent: made on first use.

send.doc: A message in their own chat. attachments are upload ids; pasted is what was pasted rather than typed. A new thread starts in project (for a member, one shared with them); folder and clear are the owner's and refused to a member. budget (a group only) is how many agent turns the message may cause, rounds included; default 10.

thread.doc: A thread's replies (its newest 500); the root is in the main chat.

history.doc: A page of the main chat, newest first before beforeSeq.

newSession.doc: The agent starts a new session.

unsend.doc: Takes back a message that still waits for its turn.

markRead.doc: Marks the chat read, or the thread threadId; all marks every place.

stop.doc: Stops the turn where the user pressed it: the chat, or the thread threadId; all stops the bot everywhere.

upload.doc: One chunk of a file for a later send, through the chat's own upload folder: base64 data at offset.

readUpload.doc: A sent file, back in chunks (chat previews on other devices).

react.doc: Toggles one emoji on an entry of their own chat.

respondPermission.doc: Answers an agent's permission card in their own chat; only a member of that agent may (a guest's go to the owner).

editHandoff.doc: Edits a handoff card's text while it is a draft.

keepConversation.doc: Keeps the conversation a handoff card offered to move on from.

makeTopic.doc: Folds the room from entryId (a message of botId's chat, or a task or thread reply in it) up to its newest line into a topic card titled title, stored as data.topic on that entry. A view over existing messages: no turn, no new line, nothing re-parented. Refused for an empty or over-80-character title, an entry of another chat, an entry inside a topic, a range holding another topic's first message, or an entry that already starts a topic.

renameTopic.doc: Retitles the topic that starts at entryId (the same title rules as makeTopic).

unfoldTopic.doc: Takes data.topic off the entry that starts a topic: its lines show in the room again.

projects.doc: Only the project folders the owner shared with them.

threadProjects.doc: The project of their own chat's thread (threadId; the main chat without it).

setThreadProjects.doc: Corrects their own chat's thread's project set, to projects shared with them; an empty list is no project.

linkCode.doc: The code that links their own Telegram, Discord or Slack account to their person.

scheduleMessages.doc: Whether their own Schedule cards are also said in their Telegram, Discord or Slack chat with the agent (on unless they turn it off), set first when on is given. The card in the app and a run's own messages stay either way.

callAccept.doc: Answers an incoming call from their own agent; the host checks the call is theirs.

callDecline.doc: Declines an incoming call from their own agent.

callGreet.doc: The call is up: the agent says what it called about.

logCall.doc: The app logs the end of a call it took as a line in the chat (frees the person for the next call).

startCall.doc: A call that just connected: its line goes in the chat now; endCall fills in its length.

endCall.doc: The call's end: its length on its line (entryId), or, for a call that never connected, only freeing the person.

createBotInvite.doc: Invites a bot guest from what they hold (docs/kith-bot-guests.md), or a new invite for their bot botId.

revokeBotInvite.doc: Revokes an invite of one of their bots.

myBots.doc: Their own bot guests, newest first.

setBotLimits.doc: One of their bots' limits; a limit left out stays. turnTimeoutS is clamped to 30 to 3600. wakeProfile (the computer's owner only) is a kith-auth profile name for the grok service; an empty string clears it.

resolveCitation.doc: A kith://thread/<id>#entry=<seq> link: the thread when it is theirs, else a stable not_shared.

proveInvite.doc: All an invited person's unproven device may call: showing the invite's token.

botStatus.doc: A bot's own state, owner and agents; also while it waits to be allowed.

proveBotInvite.doc: A bot's new key shows the invite token from its link, which the cloud never saw; until then it can call nothing else. Proving twice is fine.

botAsk.doc: Asks an agent in a conversation of the bot's own, made on first use (agent names it then). clientNonce makes a retry safe. room (a room this bot is a member of) turns the ask into one turn of the agent it @-mentions there: no conversation opens, the agent's reply wakes nobody, and an open conversation's budget is charged.

botPost.doc: Posts into a room the bot is a member of. conversation and epoch say which turn it answers; with the turnKey of the turn the room is waiting on it is the member's reply, without one it is an unprompted post (charged one turn; wakes only the members it @-mentions, only while the conversation is open with budget left). Anything else is kept as late and wakes nobody. clientNonce makes a retry post once; the same nonce with other text is nonceReused. A post never opens or tops up a budget. A room the bot is not in is notFound.

botRoomRead.doc: What a bot member may read of a room: its entries after the cursor, shaped as for a bot, with the newest conversation and epoch to post under. A room the bot is not in is notFound.

botThread.doc: What a bot may read of its own conversation, after afterSeq.

botConversations.doc: A bot's own conversations, newest first.

botStop.doc: Stops the running turn of the bot's own conversation, and the asks waiting behind it.

botLeave.doc: The bot retires itself, as if its owner removed it.

peerAgents.doc: The agents another computer of the owner's may ask here (Mac link): the owner's own, by name.

peerRevokes.doc: Mac link: the handle-only revokes and undos the caller knows. Each newer than this computer's own is applied here (the person is revoked or restored); the answer is this computer's list, so a computer that was off catches up.
